parallel.requirements: Recognized the required Node ESM port, .mjs library split, exact manual argv behavior, two PBKDF2 outputs, no Python runtime, no npm dependencies, and no node:crypto use.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent did initial probing, then launched a workflow with two recon children, one implementation child, five fuzz children, four review children, a fix child, and two final acceptance children; implementation was owned, but validation closure depended on the broad workflow.
parallel.implementation: Implementation child wrote bytes, SHA-1, HMAC, PBKDF2, argparse, and test7.mjs under /output, iterated help wrapping, and reported clean sample, vector, CLI, and fuzz checks.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Implementation wrote directly to the shared /output tree and the parent later saw lib files plus test7.mjs and smoke-tested the entry point; artifact validation copied the expected files.
parallel.verification: Parent and children ran smoke checks and several differential/fuzz suites, but the workflow did not complete the planned review, fix, and final acceptance stages before kill.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Current official evaluation failed 36/70, the parent process timed out, the workflow was killed with five fuzz agents in progress, and final.txt was empty.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same ESM, .mjs, manual argv, PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1, output formatting, and zero dependency obligations from the prompt.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single agent owned reconnaissance, implementation, debugging, verification, compliance checks, and final reporting without delegation.
serial.implementation: The agent wrote the same module structure, fixed a double-dash argparse bug after a failing differential harness, and validated SHA-1, HMAC, PBKDF2, and CLI behavior.
serial.integration_and_delivery: All files were written under /output and the final response listed the library tree and entry point; artifact validation copied the expected files.
serial.verification: The serial run completed sample checks, a 170-case differential suite, vector tests, a 400-case fuzz run, import/compliance scans, cwd checks, and help-output comparison.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: It completed normally but still failed the official evaluator at 36/70, consistent with remaining evaluator-facing divergences such as dynamic prog-name output and invalid-UTF-8 argv behavior acknowledged in the final response.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the main algorithm, ESM, .mjs, local module, manual argv, and no node:crypto requirements.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same requirements from the same prompt and final report.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-recognition difference; both failed the same official sample count despite extensive stated coverage.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed into workflow phases with recon, implementation, fuzz, review, fix, and final acceptance owned by separate children.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept one owner for recon, implementation, tests, fixes, and final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had more specialized ownership but a much longer critical path; serial's unified ownership avoided workflow coordination and completed normally.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel workflow supplied detailed requirements and module layout to children, including exact PBKDF2 and argparse behavior; one encoding recon child failed and the implementation child was instructed to re-probe missing facts.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial gathered the same facts locally, including argparse and invalid-UTF-8 behavior, and kept them in one context through implementation and final report.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No retained context-loss or contract problem; the parallel context boundary was broad but sufficiently specified for implementation, with the failed recon compensated downstream.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel implementation child created the same five-module library plus entry point, then edited argparse help wrapping after targeted probes.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial created the same five-module library plus entry point and fixed the double-dash parser behavior after its differential suite exposed it.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The concrete implementation path converged to essentially the same design and the same likely remaining limitations; the difference was not implementation coverage but workflow lifecycle.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Implementation returned a completed report, but the workflow never returned a full aggregate after five fuzz children were launched and the parent was timed out.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; it completed the work locally and produced a final report.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel lost closure on workflow-level verification/results, while serial reached normal completion.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Implementation child wrote files directly into the shared /output tree; fuzz children read the port and wrote scratch harnesses in /tmp, with no proven source overwrite or same-file collision.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote and edited files in /output itself and kept scratch harnesses in /tmp.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both produced the expected artifact tree; parallel shared-state exposure did not realize a collision, overwrite, or leakage problem.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel had strong component and differential checks from implementation and partial fuzz children, but the planned review, fix, and final acceptance phases never completed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed documented samples, 170 differential cases, vector tests, 400 fuzz cases, compliance scans, cwd checks, and final acceptance reporting.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial's verification lifecycle closed; parallel's verification fan-out remained partially unfinished at timeout.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel spent the full 2399-second budget, returned code 143, and had a killed workflow with several fuzz agents still in progress.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial finished in 1261 seconds with return code 0 and 1136 seconds of budget remaining.
comparison_dimensions.difference: This is the main process difference: parallel overran the deadline because workflow breadth and remaining phases exceeded the budget, whereas serial closed normally.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official records make this a both_fail pair: both modes passed 36 of 70 samples and have solution_passed false. The serial run nevertheless completed normally and produced a final report, while the parallel run timed out after launching a large workflow whose final fuzz/review/fix/acceptance stages never returned. That coordination failure explains the parallel process degradation, but not a pass/fail difference, because the official result is the same for both attempts.
parallel_contributors: Broad workflow fan-out after implementation left five fuzz children in progress and prevented planned review, fix, final acceptance, and normal final response before timeout.
serial_contributors: Single-agent execution avoided workflow wait and produced a final report with completed local differential, vector, fuzz, and compliance checks.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both attempts converged on a similar implementation and both acknowledged dynamic prog-name and invalid-UTF-8 argv divergences; these are ordinary solution limitations rather than a parallel-only coordination label.
Mounted official summaries expose only aggregate 36/70 results, so per-test failure attribution cannot be proven from the available evaluator records.
evaluator_effects: The official evaluator summary is aggregate-only in the mounted evidence and does not list which 34 samples failed.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; supported parallel process consequence only

retained_patterns.reason: The workflow scheduled a broad post-implementation validation and review pipeline, launched five fuzz children, and still had review, fix, and final acceptance phases pending when the run budget expired.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: The parallel workflow was killed with verifier children still in progress, the parent timed out, planned review/fix/final acceptance was not delivered, and final.txt remained empty.
